newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee steady in spot, mildly dips vs fwd dlr.
newsitem.headline: India rupee steady in spot, mildly dips vs fwd dlr.

text.p: The rupee was steady against the dollar in the spot market but was mildly down against the forward dollar on Tuesday, dealers said.
"There is lot of (dollar) selling," said a dealer.
The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) sold spot dollars in the morning session, adding to the comfortable dollar supply in the market, dealers said.
"There seems to be some leftover of yesterday's IRFC remittances," said a dealer, referring to dollar sales from a $150 FRN note raised by Indian Railway Finance Corporation.
The State Bank of India (SBI) bought dollars up to the 35.74 level, but abundant supplies kept the exchange rate steady.
The premiums were steady to mildly up in the forward dollar section as dealers looked to a repeat of Monday's Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention, dealers said.
"People are not taking positions," said a dealer.
Some analysts said RBI's forward dollar purchases were sending the wrong signals to the market and overseas investors.
"Forward premiums were getting aligned to interest rate differentials but RBI intervention is sending wrong signals," said a bank dealer.
"There is little depth in the forward market. Some banks are trying to create depth by aligning the interest rates, but RBI's latest move is confusing them," a dealer said.
"Foreign investors may also delay their remittances, thinking the higher premiums are a sign of depreciation in the offing," a dealer said.
Between July 1996 and July 1997, the rupee gained as much as 2.45 percent against the six month forward dollar, Societe Generale bank said in a foreign exchange commentary.
The RBI has said its monetary policy would be aimed at further lowering of interest rates, bank dealers said.
"It seems the RBI is in a Catch-22 situation as all efforts to weaken the rupee in the spot market are not fructifying," Societe Generale said.
